subject: Civil Engineering
title: Sheet Piles and Cofferdams
description: A quick, practical guide to Sheet Piles and Cofferdams.

hook.text: Building a bridge pier in a river means keeping water out while you pour concrete.

buildup.text: Sheet piles are interlocking steel planks driven into the ground to form a wall.

discovery.text: A cofferdam is a ring of sheet piles that creates a dry workspace in open water.

twist.text: Water still seeps under the piles. Pumps run continuously to keep the area dry.

climax.text: The Hoover Dam's cofferdams diverted the entire Colorado River during construction.

punchline.text: Wall off the water, pump it dry, and build in the open.

quiz.question: What is the purpose of a cofferdam?
options: To permanently dam a river for hydroelectric power
To create a temporary dry workspace in water for construction
To store excavated soil during foundation work

details.summary: Sheet piles are interlocking steel sections driven into the ground to form continuous walls for excavation support, waterfront structures, and cofferdams. Cofferdams are temporary watertight enclosures in rivers or harbors that allow construction in the dry by excluding water from the work area.
details.whyItMatters: Sheet piles and cofferdams enable construction in and near water, making possible the building of bridge foundations, port facilities, and dams that require work below the water surface.
takeaways: Interlocking sheet pile sections form a continuous water-resistant wall
Cofferdams exclude water from underwater construction areas
Cellular cofferdams use circular sheet pile cells filled with granular material

faq.question: How do sheet pile interlocks provide a watertight connection?
faq.answer: Sheet piles have machined interlocking profiles along their edges that slide together during driving. While not perfectly watertight, the interlocks significantly reduce water flow. For applications requiring near-zero seepage, interlocks can be sealed with sealants or welded after driving.

faq.question: What is a cellular cofferdam and when is it used?
faq.answer: A cellular cofferdam consists of circular sheet pile cells filled with granular material, creating a massive gravity structure that resists water pressure.
